title: Auto-Update Failures
description: Fix WordPress core, plugin, and theme auto-updates that fail silently or leave the site in maintenance mode.

steps.title: Identify What Failed to Update
steps.instructions: Check Dashboard → Updates for available vs failed updates. Review Site Health and email notifications. Note if core, plugin, or theme update caused the failure.

steps.title: Remove Stale .maintenance File
steps.instructions: Failed updates often leave .maintenance in the WordPress root. Delete it via SFTP if the site shows 'Briefly unavailable for scheduled maintenance'.

steps.title: Fix File System Permissions
steps.instructions: Auto-updates need write access to wp-content, plugins, and themes. Verify ownership and permissions. Use FTP/SSH credentials in wp-config if direct writes fail.

steps.title: Check Disk Space and Inode Quota
steps.instructions: Full disk causes partial updates — mixed file versions and fatal errors. Free space and retry the update.

steps.title: Complete Update Manually
steps.instructions: Run the failed update manually from Dashboard or via WP-CLI: wp core update, wp plugin update --all. Verify site works before re-enabling auto-updates.

steps.title: Disable Auto-Update for Problem Component
steps.instructions: If one plugin consistently breaks auto-updates, disable auto-update for it and update manually on staging first. Document in client maintenance notes.

steps.title: Configure FS_METHOD if Needed
steps.instructions: Add define('FS_METHOD', 'direct') to wp-config if updates fail with permission errors and the server supports direct writes. Use FTP constants only as fallback.

steps.title: Verify Updates Complete Successfully
steps.instructions: Confirm all components show current versions. Test site functionality and monitor error logs for 24 hours after the fix.
